Additional comments:

Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Long response time - can be challenging with deadlines to uphold.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Hard. Look further outside of the city.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Long commute, but good bike lanes - a fun and cheap way.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Expensive and hard to get. Got an offer from the university very late after I had found my own housing.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
What kind of help was available? *
How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very... changed all my courses in welcoming week.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Did both 1st, 2nd and 4th year courses. Great with a combination as the style of teaching is very different to uni of Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Different. Less critical and more repetition and reproduction of knowledge. Especially in year 1 and 2.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Invitation to Sociology (SCIL08017)
Ancient Literature from a Comparative Perspective (CLTR10019)
Urbanism and the City: Past to Present (ARHI08010)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: It was super fun taking a course at the Classics department. It is a well-renowned school at the university, and the people were lovely. You have to be proactive about getting a course there, as they usually have many prerequisites and do not appear in the course finder. Ask staff.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Find people that interest you and go with them to things happening in the city.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The music scene - lots of good concerts.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be openminded. Be patient in the beginning. Engage with full-time students - they know whats up and where yo go.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Openminded in terms of courses - you are last priority as a visiting student, so lower your expectations.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met and friendships made.
